text.aria-label: Title text 'Figure 12: At lead-day 14, B0's error is 1.2 points above the earlier- years climatology's, and a random-day lag gains too'
text.tspan: Figure 12: At lead-day 14, B0's error is 1.2 points above the earlier-
years climatology's, and a random-day lag gains too

text.aria-label: Subtitle text 'Top: each arm's mean absolute error minus B0's at the same lead-day, in percentage points of capacity; below zero beats B0. Line: 95% interval from resampling whole months. Bottom: the mean absolute error of B0, L1, and two climatologies, in percentage points of capacity; smaller is better. The earlier-years climatology is drawn at lead-days 1, 7, 10, and 14 only, on the 26718 rows (at lead-day 14) where it exists; its difference to B0 at lead-day 14 is -1.17 points, 95% interval [-1.82, -0.50]. A random-day lag (N2) gains at the longest lead too, so part of the lag arms' long-lead gain is not specific to recent days.'
text.tspan: Top: each arm's mean absolute error minus B0's at the same lead-day, in percentage points of capacity; below zero
beats B0. Line: 95% interval from resampling whole months.
Bottom: the mean absolute error of B0, L1, and two climatologies, in percentage points of capacity; smaller is
better. The earlier-years climatology is drawn at lead-days 1, 7, 10, and 14 only, on the 26718 rows (at lead-day
14) where it exists; its difference to B0 at lead-day 14 is -1.17 points, 95% interval [-1.82, -0.50].
A random-day lag (N2) gains at the longest lead too, so part of the lag arms' long-lead gain is not specific to
recent days.

text.aria-label: Title text 'Lead-day is the number of days between the weather forecast run and the target day. The weather forecast is the mean of the ensemble (ENS) from the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF). Fits are per plant, at the primary setting (depth 6, learning rate 0.05, 500 rounds, and row subsampling 0.8). 0*: lead-day 0 is not usable for its early hours in a live service. The saved climatology reads other blocks of months, later months included, so a live service could not make it. The earlier- years climatology reads earlier years only. The earlier-years rows are post hoc, written after the first run's results were known. All other rows are exploratory. Arms. B0: the baseline with no lag. L1: B0 plus the power at the same hour on the latest whole day before the forecast was issued (two days before the target day for a day-ahead forecast). W7: the minimum, maximum, and mean of the same hour over the last 7 whole days. Q30: the 30-day 90th percentile and median of the same hour. T1: days since the record began. Month- block folds interleave, so trees can interpolate a scored month's level from months on both sides; its gain is what interpolation buys, never drift a live forecast could use. N2: a random day from months not being scored (a null control). climatology (uses later months): the median power of the plant's calendar month and hour from the other blocks of months, later months included, with no fit. past-only climatology: the median power of the plant's same calendar month and hour in earlier years only, from its record since 2019, with no fit.'
text.tspan: Lead-day is the number of days between the weather forecast run and the target day. The weather forecast is the mean of the
ensemble (ENS) from the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF). Fits are per plant, at the primary
setting (depth 6, learning rate 0.05, 500 rounds, and row subsampling 0.8).
0*: lead-day 0 is not usable for its early hours in a live service.
The saved climatology reads other blocks of months, later months included, so a live service could not make it. The earlier-
years climatology reads earlier years only. The earlier-years rows are post hoc, written after the first run's results were
known.
All other rows are exploratory.
Arms. B0: the baseline with no lag. L1: B0 plus the power at the same hour on the latest whole day before the forecast was
issued (two days before the target day for a day-ahead forecast). W7: the minimum, maximum, and mean of the same hour over
the last 7 whole days. Q30: the 30-day 90th percentile and median of the same hour. T1: days since the record began. Month-
block folds interleave, so trees can interpolate a scored month's level from months on both sides; its gain is what
interpolation buys, never drift a live forecast could use. N2: a random day from months not being scored (a null control).
climatology (uses later months): the median power of the plant's calendar month and hour from the other blocks of months,
later months included, with no fit. past-only climatology: the median power of the plant's same calendar month and hour in
earlier years only, from its record since 2019, with no fit.
